MODERN RAILWAY CLUB'S EXHIBITION AT KINGSWAY HALL.
Experts, young and old, revealed in the Model Railway Club's Exhibition at the Kingsway Hall, W.C. Many of the exhibits were made by engine-drivers. The largest on which free rides were given, can draw nine men.
Photo shows. A lesson on different types of locomotives, being illustrated to an absorbed audience.
MODEL ENGINE DRAWS TWO MEN.

This powerful model of a South Western railway engine, is capable of drawing the weight of two men - somewhat precariously balanced on the tender. This is being shown at the exhibition in London of the Model Railway Club.
The Engine made by Mr J.C.Crebbin, which can pull nine men, at the Kingsway Hall, when the Model Railway Club held their exhibition of models. (April 25th)
WATCHING 300 MILES OF TRAINS.

In connection with the centenary year of British railways, an interesting feature of the Wembley Exhibition is the demonstration of control and signalling controls. Trains on 300 miles of line can be "watched" on the control board, where electric lights indicate their progress.
Photo shows;- The reproduction of a control on which small lights show the position of the trains.

VILLAGE DOLIMAKERS:

Two lady artists are developing the Braxted (Essex) Doll village industry, cottagers make delightful dolls in their homes, and their work has been so successful that thousands are now being produced. Foreigners have approached some of the workers with the object of finding the secret of the composition used in the moulding of the dolls heads. Trained teachers visit the cottages to give lessons in the moulding, body and wigg-making, dressing and painting of the dolls.
Photo shows...Packing dolls at Braxted ready for dispatch to distant parts of the world.
